guard: the reaper kills what carries the smoke token and leaves every other broker alone
why: THE OBVIOUS MUTATION IS DELIBERATELY NOT USED HERE, and the reason is worth more than the
mutation would have been. The natural way to prove the token filter is to delete it, so the
reaper claims every nats-server it can see. That mutation is correct in principle and dangerous
in practice: mutation-proof runs the real suite against the real machine, and on a developer box
that mutation does not fail a test, it kills every unrelated broker on the host. Measured on one
box while writing this: 15 live nats-server processes, of which the reaper claims 1. An
over-match mutation would have killed the other 14, several of them belonging to other people's
work. A test that damages the machine to prove a point is not a test worth running.
SO THE FILTER IS MUTATED BY SWAPPING WHICH TOKEN IT SELECTS ON, not by removing it. That keeps
the blast radius inside this suite's own two fixture brokers while still grading exactly the
property under test: that the surviving broker survives BECAUSE of what its path says and not by
accident of ordering, timing, or the reaper simply killing the first thing it found. It flips
both controls at once, which is the point. A mutation that reddened only the positive control
would leave open that the reaper kills indiscriminately and the negative control never noticed.
THE SECOND MUTATION SEPARATES REPORTING FROM ACTING. The reaper both kills a process and returns
a list naming it, and those are two claims that a single green cell could conflate. Removing the
kill while leaving the bookkeeping intact reddens the positive control alone and leaves 'the
killed broker is named in the report' green, which is precisely the false green this file exists
to make impossible: a reaper that reports a clean sweep it never performed.

mutations.name: the filter selects on the control prefix instead of the smoke token, so the wrong broker is claimed
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: NEGATIVE CONTROL: the untokened broker is untouched
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: NEGATIVE CONTROL: the untokened broker is untouched

mutations.name: the reaper reports the kill without performing it
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: POSITIVE CONTROL: the token-carrying broker is killed
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: POSITIVE CONTROL: the token-carrying broker is killed
